San Salvador is the capital of El Salvador. The city was founded by Gonzalo de Alvarado in 1546. It lies in the Valle de las Hamacas valley at the foot of Quezaltepeque volcano and has suffered numerous earthquakes throughout its history.

San Salvador is the country's main industrial center. Colonial buildings survive amid modern high-rises. Major sights include the Metropolitan Cathedral and El Rosario Church.

San Salvador has museums, cultural centers, theaters, bars and cafés, as well as several large markets.

Santa Ana was founded in 1569 as Cihuatehuacan, a name translated as “place of the holy woman.” The city has been known by its current name since 1708.

The city is a center of coffee production and trade. Trips to coffee farms with tastings of local coffee depart from Santa Ana.

Among the city's main sights are its neo-Gothic cathedral and El Calvario Church. To the south lies Lake Coatepeque, home to a summer resort. To the west is Tazumal, a complex of ruins of an ancient Indigenous city in modern-day Chalchuapa.

Santa Ana works well both as a destination in its own right and as a base for exploring western El Salvador.

The Santa Bárbara cenotes lie near the village of Homún on the Yucatán Peninsula. The site includes open natural pools as well as pools inside limestone caves. The water and rock walls look different in each cenote.

Paths connect the cenotes. Tours from Mérida include swimming and walking or riding between the pools. Such a trip reveals the natural side of Yucatán after exploring its cities and archaeological sites.

In the interior of Santa Cruz, travelers encounter giant land tortoises amid greenery. You can watch them from the ground and clearly see their heavy shells, how their legs move and how each animal chooses its grass.

The highlands complement the ocean-focused side of the Galápagos. On Ada Tours' diving itinerary, travelers stop here with a guide while traveling from Baltra Airport to the Fiesta Hotel. Lunch is included after meeting the tortoises, and then preparation for the dives begins.
